objective:
The Electron POS terminal calls two server routes that now exist and return correct data, and it
cannot read either response. The wire is snake_case (as every route in this API is); the terminal's
declared types `RendererPackage` and `RendererReservation` are camelCase (as everything inside the
terminal is); and `handler-deps.ts` returns `serverCall(...)` straight through for exactly these two
calls, with none of the mapping that `resolveLoyaltyMember` and `quoteLoyaltyRedemption` beside them
both have. `serverCall` is typed `Promise<unknown>`, so the cast to the renderer type is unchecked
and nothing complains at compile time.

The user-visible consequences today, at a real till:

1. Every scanned package label reports "This item has no price and cannot be sold. Ask a manager to
   price it." — `register.ts` tests `found.unitPrice` against `/^\d+\.\d{2}$/`, the wire carries
   `unit_price`, so the check runs against `undefined` and the route's most careful refusal fires on
   every item in the shop.
2. A pickup order loads as a broken cart: `catalogItemId`, `unitPrice` and `lineTotal` all arrive
   `undefined`, and the confirmation reads "Pickup order undefined loaded".
3. An expired hold classifies as ready to collect. `classifyReservation` decides from `expiresAt`,
   `pickupSlotEnd` and `isAbandonedHold`; given a body carrying none of those names every branch
   falls through and returns `ready`. The till would offer to ring a hold whose stock the expiry
   sweeper may already have returned to the floor.

This matters because these are steps 3 and 5 of an eleven-step demo walk — the two things a register
does before it can do anything else — and both have been recorded as working on the strength of
unauthenticated probes that only ever saw a 401.

Your job is the mapping and the test whose absence is the actual defect. The server half is already
done on the base branch: `pickup_slot_start`, `pickup_slot_end` and `is_abandoned_hold` were not on
the wire at all and now are.

services/alert_mailer/main.py is the single delivery path for GitHub Actions budget alerts, GCP
Cloud Billing budget breaches and cron-policy violations. Three Cloud Monitoring alert policies
deliberately carry notification_channels = [] and rely entirely on this function, so a silent
misbehaviour here means nobody is told about a budget breach.

The entrypoint alert_mailer() has three branches: kind=="cron_policy", payload contains

into the Firestore state document that _should_send reads to make future send/suppress decisions.

level with enough detail to diagnose it, and must return WITHOUT writing to the Firestore state
document. Recognized payloads must behave exactly as they do today — this is a strictly narrowing
change to one path, not a redesign.
